rounds.text: Indo-City Infotech Ltd trades at a price-to-book value of just 1.13x, which sits favorably against a sector benchmark price-to-book of 2.08x [E2, E7]. The business commands a micro-capitalisation of ₹ 13.2 Cr while demonstrating exceptional historical compounding, evidenced by a 24% compounded sales growth rate over 10 years and 18% over 5 years [E3, E14, E15]. Furthermore, recent price-led signals indicate that profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 96% with a ratio of 4.69x, showing that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E56]. Conceded: the company faces near-term top-line contraction with a 3-year compounded sales growth of -34%, a trailing twelve-month sales decline of -37%, and an elevated P/E ratio of 47.1x compared to a sector benchmark of 22.92x [E1, E6, E16, E17].

Conceded: the company trades at a price-to-book value of 1.13x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.08x [E2, E7]. However, the bull's reliance on historical 10-year and 5-year sales growth of 24% and 18% [E14, E15] masks a severe, ongoing structural collapse in demand, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of -34% and a trailing twelve-month sales plunge of -37% [E16, E17]. Furthermore, the micro-capitalisation of ₹ 13.2 Cr [E3] does not protect investors from a steep valuation penalty when paying an over-inflated P/E ratio of 47.1x—nearly double the sector benchmark of 22.92x [E1, E6]. While the bull points to recent profit-led signals showing profit growth exceeding one-year price growth [E56], this metric is directly undermined by active screen warnings flagging a 20% year-over-year sales decline and decelerating earnings growth [E71, E72]. Finally, the absence of any shareholder return through a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] leaves investors holding a contracting business with no income cushion while paying double the sector's earnings multiple [E1, E6].
